Private cfg(test) module imports overlay/protobuf/deletion/lineage types, row-ID codec, shared fixtures, Arrow schema, exact/public version selectors, CachedFileSize and collections. tagged_sample_manifest uses sample_manifest, sets both FRI bits and builds inline history5->0; it does not write/read a persisted dataset. All tests below are source evidence, not executed verification.

row_mutation helper selects delete fragment0 with predicate true, shared empty update transaction, or UpdateConfig with all maps absent/empty; unknown kind panics. These are small in-memory operation fixtures rather than realistic data writes.

Five rstest cases delete/update/config/project/merge build against tagged sample. Project and Merge clone unchanged schema/fragments. Each successful build must retain a reserved-name entry with identical UUID and index_version. It does not compare Any bytes, flags, all indices or resulting fragment values in these cases; comment's broader unchanged claim exceeds the precise assertions.

Overwrite fixture supplies Fragment::new(0), unchanged schema and no config/bases, then asserts final index list empty and reader FRI bit retained. Writer bit is not asserted here; no actual overwrite file data. Tests sticky bookkeeping after dropping tagged entry.

Stable-ID migration test uses unchanged Merge, migration_next_row_id Some100 and default build config against tagged history. Expects Error::NotSupported and stable row id migration message, verifying gate rejection before conversion/publication.

manifest_with_file creates live fragment0 field0/column0 V2_0 at caller path and sets paired FRI flags. translating_segment_and_entry gives id_idx bitmap{5} and history5->0. user_bitmap finds first id_idx and unwraps present bitmap clone; missing/unknown fixture would panic. No row-map IO in helpers.

in_place_rewrite constructs update by replacing shared fixture updated_fragments with empty Fragment0 and setting fields_modified; Merge creates b.lance fragment0 with caller fields castu32->i32 and column_indices[0], unchanged schema; DataReplacement builds analogous file and target0. Unknown kind unreachable. The fixture can use shape not representing valid production files; builder tests focus coverage metadata.

Three Update/Merge/DataReplacement cases rewrite field0 reached only through history5->0. Build must keep FRI UUID and leave id_idx bitmap empty. This asserts withdrawal of retired-source provenance instead of claiming destination; no scanner fallback or physical rows are executed.

Three analogous cases start user bitmap{0,5}, mixing direct destination and retired source. Successful build must leave bitmap empty, preventing source provenance from rederiving stale coverage. No explicit FRI payload equality asserted in this test.

Unwalkable lineage fixture history5->0 and6->8, user bitmap{0,5,6,7}, live{0,7,8}. TaggedLineage::new(entry,None) has no ledger; direct withdrawal of fragment0/field0 leaves{7}, removing every retired source. Decode inline ledger then repeat same withdrawal leaves{6,7}; unrelated retired source survives known graph. Direct helper test does not run full manifest build or simulate external read failure.

Serving-sibling fixture creates live0/1 files, translating id_idx{5}, independent same-name sibling{1} with new UUID, and other_idx unknown bitmap None. Update field0 is constructed against that manifest. Setup distinguishes empty metadata from unknown coverage and physical segments of one logical index.

First sibling build asserts translating segment UUID/name absent, sibling bitmap unchanged and unknown segment bitmap still None. Assertions inspect selected entries rather than complete index list/FRI equality. Same-name serving sibling allows retiring emptied physical metadata; no index files deleted in this test.

Second sibling build omits serving sibling and asserts sole translating segment remains with empty bitmap as rebuild record. Following independent test history5->0 plus6->8 starts bitmap{6}, rewrites0 and asserts{6} survives. Both are local metadata assertions, not actual translated query recall.

Unreadable-history test sets fri.index_details=None, then performs in-place Update. Expects InvalidInput and history substring. Despite comment about noninline history, fixture specifically covers missing Any, not an external file descriptor/callback. Other external decode behavior must use separate tests.

Six parameter cases: direct coverage for Update/Merge/DataReplacement; unindexed field for Update/Merge; off-lineage for Update. Direct sets bitmap{0}; unindexed rewrites field1 while segment indexes0; off-lineage changes history5->7. Build operation uses same in-place fixture and tagged flag; setup intentionally isolates field/lineage choices.

All six cases require FRI UUID preserved. Direct case expects empty user bitmap; other two shapes expect original bitmap. No direct DataReplacement unindexed/off-lineage case is declared; test matrix is six selected combinations, not full3x3 Cartesian product.

User CreateIndex test adds id_idx to tagged table, asserts it exists, then finds original FRI UUID and compares Any details and fragment bitmap exactly. It covers creation only; comment's replaced/dropped behavior is not exercised in this fixture.

Three unsupported cases: UpdateMemWalState empty progress, bare Rewrite of covered fragment0 to10 with no FRI entry, and Rewrite with explicit index_version0 snapshot. Each must return NotSupported with Tagged FRI history maintenance. Bare uncovered rewrites are explicitly a separate supported case; this matrix does not reject every bare Rewrite.

Two tagged-snapshot rejection cases vary whether current table is tagged. Both construct a reserved-name new entry with cleared fields and Rewrite snapshot but no prepared assembly. Build must return InvalidInput containing must be assembled, even on initially untagged table. Current tagged fixture uses metadata shape rather than complete graph IO.

Sticky-flag-only manifest with no current index attempts v0 reserved snapshot Rewrite. Expects InvalidInput and sticky feature flag text. This pins record-form policy after entry trim; no migration or stored-history bytes are read.
